Who will help us?

The action of knowledge (Jnana Karma) is beyond intellect, beyond thought, and vast like the sky. What can the Puranas, epics, and scientific sense do when they give importance only to the intellect in such action? Even great thinkers and highly educated people are unable to evaluate and study their own lives. Without that ability, can love be sustained by merely talking about an extraordinary imaginative faculty?

Intelligence, capability, and competence are indeed necessary to maintain the richness of love. But one can never evoke love by writing commentaries on the meanings of words using only intellect, capability, and competence. Such is the nature of scholars. However, we should not mistakenly perceive the life of a scholar. In the nature of karma, while trying to maintain education, wealth, and status, if there is a setback in protecting their pride, all their thoughts will be impaired. Moreover, by destroying all the goodness of life, they will try to seek spiritual merit by preaching, singing, and writing all the knowledge they have acquired to convince the world. This is about the biggest mistake among the blunders that befall those who get carried away by the vibration of education. Whenever such a soul is born, it always comes hidden behind the guise of scholarship. Most of them will neither be able to respect the dharma of the times nor seek self-acquired merit. By then, the soul would have become highly irritable, making it impossible for the capability of the learned intellect to merge through love. Instead, they will waste time finding faults in the Puranas using logic, Vedas, and epics. Later, even if they are afflicted with some kind of disease—and not an ordinary one—their scholarly pride will not leave them. When various diseases oppress and weaken them, if there is no one to offer an inquiring mind and luck stays completely far away, then they can do nothing. However, if the rigidity of the mind decreases in their final days by calling upon God, we can consider it as the merit of some past birth. Even then, they will only believe in the worldly rules they have learned and taught. They will dismiss everyone else with contempt as ignorant. They will simply be unable to impart love.

Most of them will also reach a state where they are unable to fulfill their duties to their own children or wife. If one is a brahmachari or a sanyasi, after a lot of learning, they will end up in a situation of cursing this education. Even then, without ever seeing simplicity in their own minds, they cannot think for the goodness of life other than just sharing their education, wealth, and all subsequent aspects of life. Or even if they do think, having read, known, and learned everything, they will end up as scholars who perform the karma of a distressed human lifespan and become empty. Then, they find fulfillment—in the case of Hindus—by turning some chaff and waste into ash, smearing it on their bodies, adorning themselves with sandalwood paste and vermilion for decoration, and becoming those who explain the meaning of the divine name.

Assigning a meaning to this divine name is done like this: When Shiva was in the cremation ground, to prevent ghosts from approaching, he smeared himself with cremation ashes, held a spear and trident, and guarded the cemetery. This is the story told by one group. The story told by another group is different. That is, taking Shiva and Vishnu together, they apply sandalwood paste in place of Vishnu and a vermilion dot inside it. This is the meaning of the name that has come to represent Shaivite, Shakta, and Vaishnavite! Hindu scholars assign other meanings to this as well. When similarity was attained in the father's seed and the mother's blood, the Vaishnava concept provided coolness, touching it as the seat of the mind and instilling love. When they get exhausted going after all this, some find another theory and seek refuge in it.

Do not assume that any of this is being rejected. We have a familiarity with practicing and following whatever changes and transformations have occurred in any religious doctrine from ancient times. Other than this, what else do we have? The difficulty faced when encountering experienced people is also immense. Whether the karmic path acquired over many births exists or not, when the liberationist and the rationalist come with their acquired good thoughts, this experienced person drags them into a karma that suffocates and frustrates them.

What kind of person is an experienced one? Those who have experienced yakshis, ghosts, madans, and mantramurthis with a very special devotion are also experienced people. They can also perform some miraculous deeds. There are some who have given experiences in the lineage of gods and goddesses and in the lineage of prophets. We might also experience things in the way they learned and experienced them. Seeing this as the truth, they will attach their lives to it and proceed. There is no shortage of people who discuss good deeds by telling and making others listen to the histories of great men as examples. After all, they have the experience of making others experience these things. There is also no shortage of karma where the mind itself is lost in the light of misfortune, unable to utilize it for liberation.

If there are such flaws in everything, how will we understand the truth? There is only one correct path to state for this. Do not set out to just learn and understand. Even if it is little knowledge, we have many experiences of seeking the light of experience. We must understand all this and make a decision. Each item is a completion of the good and bad karmic paths seen in this world. Due to the variations in the habit of thinking, it merely appears changed and turned in different ways. Therefore, if my soul exists, by the grace of God, I will find a personality who knows the dharmas of the era and becomes a vessel for realization. Aurobindo is someone who found it that way. There is no other medium for this.

In return for calling upon God for a long time, five gurus known as Kalantara Gurus (Gurus across time) will come, who correct things according to the times without mixing up the disembodied and the manifested. Only they will help us. The aforementioned decision is what makes us capable of seeking the path of these gurus.

If we fail to understand our ignorance about the dharma of our era and the state of becoming like a headless person, unable to impart dharma while staring at the karma of direct inferences, we will rot and decay in a deep pit similar to or even harsher than the pit of meaning-interpretation where water stagnates and termites and insects fall and rot. There is no solace for this in the theories of scholars and the ignorant. Believe that the scholars and the ignorant, who explain the meaning of the non-existent word 'Maya' by attaching it behind nihilism, cannot find a solution to this.

Only the Kalantara Guru, who seeks the meaning by exploring the action-domain (Karma Kanda) of the knowledge sheaths through the five senses, five elements, and five sheaths, can attain this. That guide will be a follower of the Yuga Dharma, discovering a long-term familiarity of seeing meanings by giving due greatness and respect to everything without rejecting anything.

How can we understand such a person? It is not about recognizing them. It is something that comes to us through our long-term fortune. That is, the period determined as Satya Yuga, Treta Yuga, Dwapara Yuga, and Kali Yuga, where a life functioned together starting from tiny creatures to the five senses, five elements, and five sheaths—this is what is meant by 'long time' (Kaladeergham). Only such a great soul can explain this to us.

We have had many scholars for a long time who speak about letters and their associated meanings. Similarly, there have been Kalantara Gurus who have spoken about devotion, yoga, karma, and knowledge. If we happen to get a birth during the times when such Kalantara Gurus are born, through our life, we will be able to discover the numerous souls standing with the dharma of the times, with our physical eyes and with inherent purity. It will also show us what these souls have attained in the five senses and the five elements. That fortune is obtained from an ideal and timely visionary whose presence comes into the experience of millions of people. A true Guru is one who points out that even for religious scholars and our predecessor renunciates who guided the time cycles of gods and goddesses, the dharma of liberation is of no use because they do not know the dharma of the time.

The time cycle of gods and goddesses refers to the Treta Yuga and Dwapara Yuga. Sri Krishna is the one who was born at the end of the Dwapara Yuga. The author of the Gita, who was a wise man by birth, himself has spoken about this time cycle. We also have many karmic paths that have been believed upon knowing that. Krishna, standing as Arjuna's Guru, made great scholars and experienced people like Drona and Bhishma fight and win the eighteenth battle known as the Kurukshetra war. When it is said that even through such an Arjuna, due to the ignorance of the Shudra class and the scholarly dharma of the elite scholars, the Kalantara Guru path where Shudras, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Brahmins worked together could not be sustained, whom will we hold onto? How will we hold on? This should be our thought.

Sri Krishna is not the supramental radiance. Aurobindo Ghosh has said that it is the overmind bringing the supramental radiance into the land of temporal dharma. What should we see here? Only if we get an opportunity to be born, grow, and be nurtured during the period when a Dharma Guru is born, will we be able to understand the essence of the Yuga Dharma that has evolved over four eras. If we do not get a great soul who has attained the temporal dharma to be born into that karmic path, then we will never get the opportunity to discover this meaning.

When we look at the many Gurus who came and went, like Buddha, like many other Gurus who sought only the truth, and like the prophets who knew the subtlety of the celestial dharma, we must also consider at this juncture that even they had to return without being able to find this essence.
Guruvani
Guru Jayanti Edition
September 1999
Our Tradition is an Unbearable Burden

You might have some part of faith in you. But one should handle faith only after knowing its cause and effect. I am talking from my own experience. If someone suddenly jumps in and shows a siddhi (supernatural power), like blessing and cursing everything away, nothing will come of it, and nothing is going to happen here. People have some fake tricks in their hands like siddhis, illusions, and blessings. If one blesses and sends using such fake tricks, the prosperity of the house will only be lost. Moreover, when the children grow up, they will grow into utter wickedness.

What is our need today? We have a karma that we have been doing until this very moment today. That karma has purity, it has a truth, it has everything. Do this only after knowing it. Do not just blindly believe it because someone says so. That is not right. God Himself will give us the knowledge and experience to achieve this. We should not throw away what God gives us. Whatever God gives is useful for all of you.

Whoever you are, you are people who have lived based on a belief. This is not about any particular religion or caste. When that belief went astray in some way, religious doctrines came in and further distorted, preached, and propagated it—thus, the karmic path of that doctrine also became unknown. Each of us is the remainder of such an outdated karma. No one should assume that it will be fixed immediately. The hardships of some people, according to their willingness to suffer, will gradually reduce and then suddenly decrease. Then, where a huge destruction was supposed to happen, maybe just a finger will get cut. That is not to be considered a big deal. For example, instead of a severe fever, a mild fever and cough that puts one in bed for four days will come. At that time, you shouldn't say, "Oh, trouble has come, I am very distressed," this is not what should be said; all these are bound to happen. And it will pass on its own way.

Our subject is this - how will this old karmic path of ours end, how should it be ended? If someone says that this karmic path, which I and my ancestors have spoken, practiced, done, and made others do until today, does not exist, it will not end. To say it will just end like that is foolishness. Wherever and whatever we have been doing, it will not end suddenly. But we have God's grace. A permanent solution for that old karma which we have been doing knowingly or unknowingly until today. That solution, the solution God shows us. That solution will not come unless the men, women, young, and old in the house strive together equally. If someone says God has come to stay extra with him, what can be done for that house? We can only tell the extra God to leave.

Whether educated or uneducated, foolish or intelligent, capable or incapable, if everyone sees that God's greatness is one—if someone becomes arrogant thinking he has a lot of intelligence, we can only let it go its way. Nothing will come or go by being arrogant like that. If they become arrogant with education and wealth, let them be arrogant.

Each of us is the remnant of the ignorance that says, "God is rooted in my caste, God is rooted in my religion." That is, we are standing on the wrong side of knowledge. If one thinks, "Some great soul has taken away all my mistakes and the shortcomings arising from them, now I just have to sit idly," things will not work out. This mistake is not something that any great soul can just wash away.

As far as we are concerned, the karmic defect, or the quality of karma that has occurred through origin by birth - we must first come to the knowledge to experience this. Know and experience. Let the sorrow that is bound to come, come. Still, I must overcome it. This should be our goal. Saying, "Oh, I went there, everything is destined," is not knowledge. If you act upon such knowledge, unimaginable ruin will come to you. No matter how much it hurts or how much we struggle, we have to handle and overcome this.

How will we know what our ancestors have done? If we say wealth and aristocracy should come equally to everyone, it is something that will not happen anywhere in the world. As part of giving wealth to everyone, someone in the past proposed giving thirteen and a half cents of land to each person. In the past, one person got thirteen and a half cents. How many people are there today? In the future, how many will there be? This is a trick to deceive these poor people. Another group will say, "I am struggling with work." What work? Whose work? For what? What if one works for the public good? What is public good? Let each one think. The house of the one who struggles will be ruined, that's it. Some clever ones will say, "Struggled a lot, couldn't know what love is." So, these things shouldn't just be said and compromised with.

We will only receive what we are meant to get from the karma we painstakingly build with love, humility, and respect. Without love, without guidance, if someone says something and we decide to just jump into it, we will only jump. Nothing will be gained from there. Things will only happen according to the dynamics of the soul. If we say we have everything but cannot swallow a drop of water, isn't that the misfortune of the soul? Others have so many things in their hands to do for us. No one is doing anything. What to do? Will it be enough for us if someone gives us something for a day or ten days? Don't our children need to grow up? We must understand that none of this is a karma of a sense of justice. One can fabricate and say many things about the sense of justice. Destinies can be declared. But that is not the destiny of his soul. Regarding this destiny, both men and women are the same. If anyone says it is not so, it is guidance that pushes one entirely into alienation.

We see various kinds of politicians. We see various kinds of religious theorists. Is anything they say actually happening here? Does anyone need to talk about the world? It is neither the fault of those who said this, nor the fault of those who knowingly repeated what was said. Without understanding the sorrows, knowledge, experience, and depth of its past and future, just jumping in and saying something will not accomplish anything. It hasn't worked to this day either. When we have so much evidence in front of us, why are we saying and showing all these unnecessary things? Anyone making you listen to such things is unnecessary.

You all know that I am someone who has suffered a lot just like you. But I do not think about that suffering. If I think like that, can I live? It is true, there was suffering, that is its nature. God gave a dignity to that suffering. If God gives us, we should be willing to share it with everyone. That is sacrifice. For that, money, capability, wealth, everything will be needed.

What is the reason for our suffering? It is the unbearable burden of our tradition. What is that burden? Our soul's lack of dharma, lack of luck, lack of merit. Can one just go somewhere one day, throw it away, and come back? Do not say such things to anyone. What is being said is not right. These are all deceptive tricks of religious doctrines, siddhi justifications, and miraculous deeds meant to fool people. No one should ever believe these.

As for us, we have God's mercy. What is being said is the truth. But one must feel the pain for God's mercy. We might not know anything about such things. But one thing, when we finish doing good and bad deeds, we go again and perform karma according to the rules of the respective religion. And then jump around in the logic of the non-believer. Whatever anyone else does, what is it to you? That is not what I am saying. None of us should think that we can improve by acting otherwise. It is the father's fault, it is the mother's fault, it is the land's fault, it is the country's fault—what is all this? The land we were born in lacks luck. What is the reason for us being born in that place? Isn't it enough to see that we are even unluckier than that?

Yes, we are worse than everything else. Our ancestors were those who, enveloped in a huge cover of loveless actions without ever knowing what the dynamics of the soul are, danced towards destruction thinking it was love. When God gives us an opportunity to change from this, you—father, mother, husband, and wife—should never behave leaving it aside. Only then can you be saved. If you leave it, you will never be set right.

All this is a karma that can occur if we are born. If we reject all this and walk away, our dharma or karma does not become complete. Only if you do it with effort, keep a detached mind to know and remove the sins and merits that have come due to the ignorance of the ancestors, and tie love and respect along with it, will you be able to remove it. Otherwise, you will never remove it. After a while, you will abandon your faith and leave. This is a familiar experience of mine.

Let our past theories be right or wrong. We do not need to try fixing them by debating their rights and wrongs. We were born. Now, what all can we do for this? Let us think about a time when God showed us some mercy as an opportunity for this. A karmic path for us to know each other, speak, do, and make others do. That should be a love that comes towards dharma. It should not be a love where merit is lost. Destruction will happen there. In this matter, you should act with strong determination. If God gives us an opportunity to do it and make others do it systematically, it must be done. That persistence—that love and respect—must be held onto without letting go. If it goes without love, humility, and respect, everything will follow that absence. Most of our ancestors were those who went that way. We shouldn't jump around seeing that. If some miraculous deeds are shown, or the full form of siddhi paths are shown, none of it will be of use to us. We shouldn't believe in any such thing. Our love will cease to exist. Understanding this much, you must strive hard. If you waste time, you must strive hard. Otherwise, time will be lost. How many people do we see in front of us who have lost their time and opportunities like this? Some will do many things unable to bear it out of love. After a while, all their love is gone. Did a thief take it? This is all I have to say. I cannot bring you closer by talking about other things. Depending on your knowledge and love, it can be taken.

Regarding knowledge, I do not intend to thrust great knowledge upon you. Your knowledge is less, your experience is less, your familiarity is less. You don't even know what the sins and merits of your ancestors are. Let it be whatever it is. I happened to be born, happened to grow up. Or else, something will happen in this life. Let whatever happen. I need a liberation from this. That liberation should pave the way to salvation (Mukti). This should be our thought. Rather than that, there is no point in us getting agitated and jumping around hearing whatever anyone says.

Many have fallen because they did not do this knowingly. Therefore, this matter is being told straight to you. I have seen my experience to be like that. If there is knowledge in that direction, we won't face any unseemly situations. We can do whatever can be lifted up with our own love, respect, and humility.

You will experience diseases, sorrows, difficulties, and poverty in many forms. This is present in all human beings. Some do not get cured even if treated. When treated for some, another disease comes. Another one is an incurable disease. Even though we say many things as reasons for this, it is the soul's lack of merit. What can be done to cure the soul's lack of merit? It reaches a state where it cannot be grasped in any way. Even if we ask those who come as great believers and great visionaries, there is no solution. It is difficult to find such a person.

This difficulty is the same among Hindus, Christians, Buddhists, and Jains. Because, we celebrate a familiar practice we followed for a long time. When such a concept is continuously imparted, this karma becomes like a disease and a sorrow. It happens to many people like that. Nobody says what the reason for this coming is. The method of most people is to believe in whatever any of our ancestors worshipped, and occasionally go and pray. But do not assume that this will become worship of God. Worship of God means we can do it in every way; the concept is that God is in everything. It is not like that. Regarding what is called God, this concept has emerged due to the numerous mistakes made because we did not do it and understand it according to each era. It has not come because of any other shortcoming.

Many people who lived in grand ways, and that too those who lived doing many good deeds, are caught in such a concept. If it is said that the reason for all this is the soul lacking merit, will wealth and capability come to those without any merit? But how should that merit be used, in what way should it be done so that it remains as merit, what should our life turn it into—we have not learned any of this. If a little wealth or capability comes, we should live grandly, look down slightly on others, and through them, we should become big. This is what is learned. What merit does the soul have for us with this mindset? We have a past experience of living like this for crores of births. How can this be changed?

Some fall very far behind in purity of character. However, some who have a little capability, skill, and respect will carry it around as a great status and completely destroy even the merit they possess. This is an artificial construct among us.

We will live, grow, and die. What good is there for our soul? We carry around this foul-smelling body by scrubbing and bathing it. If the soul is not in this body, what will we do? If such a soul becomes like a rotten tree, what will we do? No one comes forward to say how this should be resolved. When we suffer the most, where will we go? To some astrologer, or a sorcerer, or some temple, or if some Swami is sitting somewhere, then there. No one should assume that we will get merit from these places. That assumption is not special. What is the deficiency in our soul - this is the target. How can this deficiency of the soul be changed - we do not know this at all.

What we have heard is the Trinity system, or the Prophetic system, or the path of the Guru—let it be anything, can we only go the way the word of God is received? If we go through this path, after four thousand or five thousand years, what will we be able to know about our ancestors? If we go according to the calculation of ages (Yugas), crores of matters come up according to the calculation of ages. Can we go knowing all this?

No tradition has ever taught us according to the Yuga Dharma (duty of the age). This is the reason for the shortcomings of all people. Can we immediately live according to this Yuga Dharma? No. But this is the time destined for it.

Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra—this much is stated as Varna Dharma (duty based on class). It hasn't been said whose Yuga Dharma this is for which time. Because it is taught that the Dharma of Kali (Yuga) is bad, there are people who believe that none of this should be done in this Kali Yuga. It is not like that; if this Kali is entirely meant for the Shudra, then this Shudra has the authority. That is, Kali is the time when the Shudra is entitled to Brahma Jnana (knowledge of Brahman). He can achieve it only in Kali. We must firmly establish a belief that through the Dharma of Kali, the Shudra can acquire the authority for Brahma Jnana. Otherwise, no matter which politics is spoken, which caste is spoken, or which religion is spoken, our sorrow will not be alleviated. A deficiency that ancestors followed and worshipped, regardless of which sphere they belonged to, exists for all families that have aged in life. Thinking that there is no oldness is also our ignorance.

There are many people who worship tiny gods for tiny castes and live in forests and beaches. They will not have any knowledge about what God is. When they do things based on what they have heard and seen here and there, everything will go out of rhythm. Eventually, he will die and go stand somewhere. If one dies, one shouldn't assume the soul is saved. Wherever there is life that has happened with complete ignorance, it will go and stand there.

Everyone knows that there is a sky around this earth. Beyond the layer of the earth, there are three visible exteriors - Earth, Moon, and Sun. Between these, some spheres that cannot be seen by the eye are moving. These are called Navajyothis. Or else it can be called sky or earth. There is such a calculation. Can one operate knowing all these calculations? You don't need to know any of that. All this certainly exists. Meaning, there is no need to wait to know all this before proceeding. It is impossible to go having known it like that.

I will tell you some things that you can do. When we consistently do something, the mind will go downwards. This is some deficiency of the soul. As we grow, we will act in various ways. What if a disease comes at that time? This is the soul's lack of merit. We are also unable to generate merit for this soul. This is the shortcoming of us human race. An astrologer will look and tell you to do this and that. Doing that won't make a difference.

Our ancestors who lived have become devas (gods), devis (goddesses), rishis, sanyasis, or jnanis. Where do all these stand as dead ties? Coming as their successors and dying, billions of souls are standing in zodiacs without merit. Then the children born become sickly, when they grow up they don't get what they need for their growth, they lack the ability to work and achieve—this is usually called family curse (Kudumba Dosham). But this is not just a family curse, it is also a deficiency of the soul. This must be corrected through life.

Sri Krishna is the one who came as the greatest person. How did we perceive what Krishna said? Krishna came as a jnani (wise one) by birth. No one else came as a jnani by birth. They become jnanis after coming. Not only that, by birth and origin, he was a person born after passing the position of a deva. That is why Krishna got the dark color. Sri Krishna's color is the color of the sky. Does the sky actually have a color? No. He attained a state and came as a Guru. That is how he defeated his uncles and ancestors like Drona and Bhishma in archery. Why kill them? The ancestors (Pitrus) they killed stand elsewhere. If these Pitrus continue to stand like this, if they remain alive, this war cannot be won. Therefore, he just killed them. He got Arjuna to kill them. This should be understood in this way.

We have learned that Sri Krishna is the greatest. Not just learned, it is an experience. What is known about Sri Krishna is that he is a Jnani. Being a Jnani means having no attachment to father, mother, husband, children, or anything. But there is a connection—with the truth. This is Sri Krishna. Didn't he kill his children? That is Sri Krishna's quality. Without understanding Krishna in this way, we have learned the story of sixteen thousand and eight women. In the very place where we worshipped the Deva and Devi, we are worshipping Krishna as well. This is our mistake. Sri Krishna is not such a person.

The Gopa women are those who accepted only Krishna as their Guru over many births. What is meant by sixteen thousand and eight? It is a scene in the eighth state. If Sri Krishna's soul leaves the body, then it can stand taking a form, stand without a form - and it can also scatter as atoms. That is Sri Krishna. Because we did not get the knowledge to see Sri Krishna this way, what did we do? Along with worshipping Devas and Devis, our ancestors worshipped Krishna too.
Even though Krishna came freely in this manner, his uncles could not see that greatness. Therefore, even before Sri Krishna was born, how much sorrow that family experienced!

When we say a mother, that mother will get happiness and sorrow from her children. If they fall into such a karma, that mother should become complete through that life. Not by rejecting husband, wife, and children, but by properly following the practices related to them. One shouldn't do anything by abandoning children, abandoning father, abandoning mother, or abandoning husband. Through our life, we are living out a life.
Guruvani

The Soul that is Set Aside

Throwing far away the numbness of "what must come will come, what must go will go," this is the time to think about what was destroyed in the path of trade, what was lost, where the karmic path shook and scattered, and where that karmic path lay before. Now, instead of standing divided, haggling and shrinking, what we need today is the karmic skill to step together into the realm of action and work. Because the growth and survival of our country are crucial today. We must evaluate and realize what all hardships have come to the country from our hands, and know what that hardship is that many have lost by blindly going after a reign of comfort without knowing. Otherwise, beyond the ignorance of losing oneself watching a festival and bursting crackers and laughing, how will we know what lies beyond?

Today we need Gurus and followers who instruct on how to obey and correct the karma that has come as ordained by fate. The sharpness of what each person says will increase. But from this, you must understand one thing. It is not the children in his house that he is training. Whatever castes, religions, and classes exist in the human race, they should all come together in unity, and instead of pushing away this truth that has been found and perishing in the old traditional customs, what is needed is not that. What all needs of the believers must be maintained for us to have come? Giving excessive importance to the religious and caste nature that has existed till today, praising non-existent qualities, and jointly immersing ourselves in the tantric practices that pawn our very souls—our need today is to rise from it, seek out the path to liberation, find it, and knock it open.

After stating today's need, we shouldn't go into a karma that is useless for tomorrow. What is meant by time and karma? What exists in the Treta Yuga is slightly renewed and used in the Dwapara Yuga. If the Treta Yuga is the time of the Deva, or if it is the time from the ghost to the Deva, respect and take only that realm.

What is the difference between a ghost, a Deva, and a human? Regarding the ghost, besides what is mentioned in Puranas and epics, there are many types of ghosts. There are ghosts that have gained strength coming through human karma. What these powerful ghosts do is the karma of sowing untruth in truth. At the same time, there are demonic karmas that pass with time. Like building a bridge without deciding the location, or like those who take contracts desiring profit. It doesn't mean profit is not needed. For a fish market vendor, he will only get a crore in profit if he sells to lakhs of people. The knowledge, experience, and habit of a wholesale merchant who collects and supplies goods according to the season is not the same as someone who takes and supplies goods day by day. The wholesale merchant looks at the pros and cons, calculates that an item will barely last this long, or seeing that it is something that will be lost, if it is an unusable item, he will sell it off before its time expires, by reducing or increasing the price. But a retail vendor cannot do any of this. Just as he can only do with what he has, followers of Yuga Dharmas have certain tasks that they resolve in the soul over a Yuga. Through the Satya Yuga, there are those who live, perform karma, and attain a true form according to their respective tendencies. That accumulation of form takes ages, and is executed after seeing the beginning, middle, and end forms in the meaning of a Yuga Dharma. Like a woodcutter standing in a forest or village in the beginning, bringing the cut wood to the place he intends, experiencing the difficulty of not having discovered iron or similar materials of that kind, struggling, he will somehow complete that task. When iron cannot be used to cut a dry tree in the forest, he will pluck wild vines suitable for cutting it, tie it and pull it to one side, and do whatever he can to take it to the place he intends. That karma performer knows how to bring it to some tree or level ground and process it the way it needs to be done. Similarly, he will also discover some techniques finding that each wood has a specific quality. Thus, he will perform all form-resolutions concerning the wood.

What is form-resolution? Like the growth of the mind and the thinking habit of knowledge, using that wood, he will craft the forms intended in his mind through a special power of imagination. Because, in that era, iron or other tools had not been discovered to cut and unfold them into forms, right? By the time he reaches the next Yuga, he would have sat and thought about this many times, wondering what the solution for this is. It can be seen that this is a karmic path where his own births change into many forms.

Like someone thinking about the theory of evolution, like someone discovering tools and understanding their use and nature over time, there were some great souls who sought merit through births in every subject. If they leave their bodies and it is seen that they have no interest in taking birth or anything else, God Himself will set their souls aside. Then they are born by being given the intellect and capability to come along with the discovery. When Yugas change and come, those who have worked in various ways like this will be born. Similarly, if one does not act after observing and knowing, a muteness that prevents the intellect from growing and being nurtured will grip them, and a habit of mixing up right and wrong in what they do and calling everything right will reach them. When a Yuga is completed like that, everyone from ghosts onwards will come dancing, swaying, and speaking. After that, growing as various creatures in that manner, when a Yuga is completed, a change will occur. Even those who acted in that manner in the Satya Yuga are watching our family and future.

The karmas that have evolved by changing and thinking through Yugas like this are what we see before us today. When a Chatur Yuga (cycle of four ages) passes, many will grow in this nature. They will be born here and there in various lifestyles. Thus, the special characteristics of the Yuga Dharmas can be seen through them.

This is what can be seen as a vision and directly. That will grow, and the familiarity to perform karma up to Jivanmukti (liberation while living) will be attained. In the Chatur Yugas that follow in this manner, if these aforementioned people make any mistake, they will keep going according to that mistake. They won't even know it. When many such Chatur Yugas pass, they then come as great souls who follow the Yuga Dharma. Then, for them, it will be received as if God Himself waited and told them. It will be experienced either told as a disembodied voice or in the nature of the word spoken by the author of the Gita as 'manifested dharma' through forms. But no matter what is experienced, if his knowledge becomes base, it will become evil letter by letter.

When it is said Chatur Yuga Karma, it means the first Chatur Yuga of the first Manu. This karma is completed by fourteen Manus. If one comes to the position of a Guru to complete it like that, that Guru will bring changes to every Chatur Yuga. This Guru will accomplish it by foreseeing and acting even up to natural disasters. This Guru is the complete Guru.
Guruvani
